stemMd:
Two materials perform similarly in a short laboratory test, but one deteriorates under repeated drying while the other does not. An engineer choosing a material for an outdoor structure should therefore ______.

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.label: A
options.textMd: assume equal short-test scores guarantee equal durability everywhere

options.label: B
options.textMd: reject every laboratory test as useless

options.label: C
options.textMd: consider whether the test conditions capture stresses relevant to the intended use

options.label: D
options.textMd: choose solely by the order in which the materials were tested

explanationMd: The new evidence reveals a stress that distinguishes the materials despite similar initial scores. Selection for outdoor use requires a test-to-use connection, not blind reliance on one proxy.

distractorRationale.a: The drying difference contradicts that guarantee.
distractorRationale.b: The evidence identifies a limitation, not universal uselessness.
distractorRationale.d: Test order has no stated relevance to outdoor performance.
